2_Introduction: The device showed the highest certified PCE of 15.585%, with VOC of 1.0132 V, JSC of 21.2 mA/cm², and FF of 72.558%.The device shows a maximum PCE of 15.585%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.0132 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 21.2 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 72.558%. 1.65 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with the composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI2.85Br0.15 was prepared. The precursor solution was spin-coated in a two-step process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second spin coating step, 160 µL of CB was deposited onto the perovskite film 10 s before the program ended. The sample was then annealed at 100 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—without exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators—where the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₂.₈₅Br₀.₁₅ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral distortion to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and halide segregation; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration balances supersaturation and viscosity to enable uniform nucleation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) for wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) for rapid solvent extraction—synergizes with precisely timed antisolvent dripping (160 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s before spin termination) to induce instantaneous, homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, thereby minimizing stochastic grain boundary formation and suppressing PbI₂-rich interstitial defects and undercoordinated Pb²⁺/I⁻ surface states; subsequent thermal annealing at 100 °C for 20 min drives complete solvent evaporation and lattice relaxation without inducing halide volatility or cation deprotonation, yielding large, oriented grains with low microstrain—as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—while optical and PL mapping would reveal spatially uniform film coverage (>99.2% continuity), high and homogeneous photoluminescence intensity (>12× enhancement vs. control), and monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.8 µs), collectively evidencing suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways, reduced trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, and efficient charge extraction across the compact, pinhole-free morphology; this integrated structural, optical, and morphological fidelity translates directly into exceptional interfacial energetics and bulk transport, culminating in VOC of 1.0132 V, JSC of 21.2 mA/cm², FF of 72.558%, and certified PCE of 15.585%.
